result.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
result.comment: 28 pages. Project page and code available at https://yunfeixie233.github.io/s2/
result.summary: Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, different modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To examine this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. We find that $S^2$ correlates positively with downstream robot task success across embodied model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. $S^2$ can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs). Beyond this correlation, $S^2$ offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs). With $S^2$, we extend PRH to embodied models and make sensorimotor alignment empirically measurable, offering insight into why an embodied model succeeds beyond its closed-loop success rate.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的离线度量 S²，衡量模型感官表示与物理运动几何的一致性，发现其与多类具身模型的下游机器人任务成功率正相关，可在闭环评测前筛选模型与 VLM backbone。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用表示几何对齐做能力离线代理」的思路可供核查能否迁移为诊断 LVR 内部状态是否保留任务必要视觉与运动结构，但论文面向机器人策略评测，未涉及 latent 推理状态的生成与使用，联系为方法线索而非主线。
